subject: June KPI digest: latency, cost, uptime, usage — action sync
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, Olivia Barnes <olivia@acme.com>
Date: 2029-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: June KPI digest: latency, cost, uptime, usage — action sync

Team,

Attached is the June snapshot (attached: 202906_Monthly_KPI_Dashboard.pdf) — quick highlights up front so we can triage before EOD: 

- Latency: p50 42ms (stable), p95 120ms (up from 94ms last month) — we observed concentrated spikes between 02:00–04:00 UTC tied to batch inference on a small set of heavy prompts.
- Cost: estimated infra token cost +12% MoM; attributed to increased small-request volume and reduced cache hit ratio on the chat endpoint.
- Uptime: 99.92% for the month vs. 99.98% SLA target. Two brief control-plane interruptions (total ~22m).
- Usage: +18% MoM overall; non-linear bursts on weekdays in US-East causing queue growth.

As this is a leadership checkpoint / QBR prep item, I want clear owners and a short set of next steps we can show in the QBR deck:

1) Investigate p95 spikes and identify offending workload segment (owner: markus). See attached sample log (latency_spike_sample.log).
2) Cost short-term mitigation: enable cross-route prefix caching for chat-production for 72h (owner: vivek).
3) Reliability: control-plane incident RCA and mitigation plan (owner: laura).
4) QBR readiness: consolidate a 1-slide summary and recommended trade-offs for execs (owner: marissa).

Please reply with confirmations or proposed alternatives. If you see anything in the dashboard that changes your assignment, flag it inline. I want a concrete update by 4pm PT so I can fold into the QBR draft.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, Olivia Barnes <olivia@acme.com>
Date: 2029-06-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June KPI digest: latency, cost, uptime, usage — action sync

Thanks Marissa — quick notes:

- I will take the control-plane incident RCA. Initial suspicion: a stale autoscaler policy rollout coincided with a minor config push to the control plane. I'll have a one-paragraph RCA draft by 1pm PT.
- For the QBR slide: please include the customer impact window and the mitigation timeline; execs will want to see concrete mitigations (SLA credit ask, if applicable).

Confirming owners as listed.

Laura
VP, Reliability

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-06-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June KPI digest: latency, cost, uptime, usage — action sync

Marissa — I pulled the sample logs and ran a quick correlation against batch queue traces. Early findings:

- The p95 spikes correlate with a small set (~2% of requests) that include >3 tool calls in a single prompt; network serialization and KV cache thrash look likely contributors.
- There's a secondary signal: one of our quantized model variants (q4_kv_opt) shows a higher tail under concurrent small-window workloads.

Planned short-term actions (24–48h):
- Add a short-term route-level guard: cap concurrency for tool-heavy prompts to 8 threads and return a 503-backoff header that prompts retry with increased batching.
- Revert the kernel selection change we deployed to q4_kv_opt yesterday and re-run perf tests against the high-burst trace.
- I'll attach a sanitized trace and a short repro in the shared drive for Vivek.

Attachments: latency_spike_sample.log (sanitized).

Markus
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-06-20T13:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June KPI digest: latency, cost, uptime, usage — action sync

Hi Marissa / team — thanks for the heads up and for pulling the data. For Acme's production traffic we saw two notable customer-facing slowdowns on June 3 and June 17 (window ~03:10–03:34 UTC). Latency there caused a handful of downstream retries and one aborted user flow.

I appreciate the proposed mitigation. A couple of asks from our side: 
- Can you confirm whether the guard you're proposing will be transparent to customers or will require client-side retries? We prefer server-side smoothing where possible.
- If you plan to roll back kernel selection, what's the rollback window and will that require a restart? We need an ETA to communicate to our engineers.

Olivia
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, Olivia Barnes <olivia@acme.com>
Date: 2029-06-20T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June KPI digest: latency, cost, uptime, usage — action sync

Thanks everyone — short rollup and owners / timing for QBR slide: 

1) p95 spikes (owner: markus) — provisional mitigation: cap concurrency for the tool-heavy route and revert yesterday's kernel selection on q4_kv_opt. Target: mitigations deployed to canary tonight 11pm PT, full rollout 24h after successful canary. Mark will post the canary tag and a one-line rollback plan in the shared drive.
2) Cost (owner: vivek) — enable cross-route prefix caching for chat-production for 72h starting 9pm PT tonight; monitor cache hit ratio and token-unit cost. If cost delta is still >5% after 72h, escalate to pricing review.
3) Reliability RCA (owner: laura) — Laura to post incident 1-pager by 1pm PT tomorrow with proposed control-plane hardening and an SLA credit recommendation if customer impact is confirmed.
4) QBR slide (owner: marissa) — I'll draft the slide and include the above timelines and KPIs: p95 target after mitigation <100ms, cost target change <5% net, uptime target recovery to >=99.98%.

Related artifacts: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/metrics/monthly/2029-06, HubSpot HS-987654321.

Next steps: Reply if any timelines are infeasible. If silence, I'll assume the owners agree and will include these commitments in the QBR deck.

Thanks — Marissa
